title: India Beat Pakistan 3-2 In SAFF Opener After Late Stoppage-Time Scare
excerpt: Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored twice in the first 19 minutes and Manglenthang Kipgen added a third before half-time as defending champions India held on in Dhaka after Pakistan struck twice in stoppage time.
body:
• India beat Pakistan 3-2 in their SAFF Championship 2026 Group B opener at the National Stadium in Dhaka on November 5.
  • Suhail Ahmad Bhat scored in the 13th and 19th minutes; Manglenthang Kipgen made it 3-0 in the 31st.
  • Pakistan's Najeeb Ullah (90+1) and Alamgir Ghazi (90+4) scored in stoppage time but could not complete the comeback.
  • India top Group B with three points and next face Maldives on November 11 in Dhaka.

DHAKA — Defending champions India began their SAFF Championship 2026 campaign with a 3-2 victory over Pakistan in a Group B match at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Thursday, November 5, surviving a late fightback after leading 3-0 at half-time.

Suhail Ahmad Bhat struck a brace, scoring in the 13th and 19th minutes, while Manglenthang Kipgen struck in the 31st minute, according to reports by MyKhel and Khel Now.

Bhat's early brace sets the tone

India started patiently, retaining possession and building through midfield. Bhat first thought he had scored in the 12th minute, but the effort was ruled out for offside.

A minute later he had his goal. Muhammad Suhail collected a throw-in on the left flank and delivered a cross into the area, and Bhat converted from close range. India doubled the lead in the 19th minute when Abhishek Suryavanshi played a through ball behind the Pakistan defence and Bhat finished first-time past goalkeeper Yousuf Butt.

Kipgen extended the lead in the 31st minute. Noufal PN carried the ball forward and released Kipgen, who raced into the penalty area and beat the advancing goalkeeper to make it 3-0.

Pakistan had a chance to cut the deficit before the break when Suryavanshi fouled Hayyaan Khattak in the box, but Shayak Dost sent the penalty over the crossbar. Bhat also came close to a hat-trick before half-time, his long-range attempt missing narrowly.

"Bhat first thought he had scored in the 12th minute, but the effort was ruled out for offside."

Control after the restart, then a nervy finish

India continued to create chances after the restart. Adison Singh Thokchom was denied in a one-on-one, while Kipgen and Farukh Choudhary also came close, but the defending champions could not add a fourth goal.

That left the door open, and Pakistan pushed through it in stoppage time. Najeeb Ullah headed home a cross from Junaid Shah in the 91st minute. Three minutes later, Alamgir Ghazi controlled a cross from McKeal Abdullah and produced an acrobatic finish to make it 3-2.

India held on for the final moments to take all three points.

What it means for Group B

The win puts India top of Group B with three points and a goal difference of +1, Khel Now reported. The top two teams from each group progress to the semi-finals.

India next face Maldives on November 11 at 3:00 PM at the National Stadium in Dhaka, in what Khel Now described as their final Group B fixture.

The result gives the defending champions the start they wanted, but the closing minutes are the lesson: a side that controlled most of the match for an hour still had to defend a one-goal lead at the end after conceding twice in added time. Managing that late phase will matter more as the tournament tightens, starting with Maldives.
